summary: A window over the page that holds focus until it is closed. It wraps the browser's own dialog element.

open.description: It is showing. A script adds and removes it.

alert.description: The dialog interrupts with a message that needs an answer: it gets the alertdialog role.

root.note: Takes no room; the panel part shows in the top layer.

panel.note: A native dialog element the author writes and marks with data-part="panel". The browser makes the rest of the page inert, keeps focus inside, and closes on Escape.

title.note: Inside the dialog: the heading the dialog is named after.

description.note: Inside the dialog: the text the dialog is described by. An alert dialog needs one.

keys.Escape: Closes the dialog (the browser does this).
keys.Tab: Moves among the dialog's controls and stays inside it (the browser does this).

events.close: The dialog element's own event, dispatched when it closes; its returnValue says which button closed it.

guidance.text: A button inside a form with method="dialog" closes the dialog, as in plain HTML. When it opens, focus goes to the element the author marked with autofocus, or else to the first control; when it closes, focus returns to where it was.

notYet: Closing on a press outside the dialog.
A dialog that is not modal.
